claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely matched derivative has high saturation magnetization and coercivity no greater than about 100 Oe.
Controlled isothermal aging can induce nanoscale, coherent, ordered secondary-phase precipitates in an fcc FeCoNi-based matrix.
A suitable aging temperature and duration can form the precipitates without disrupting the overall fcc matrix structure.
The resulting coherent precipitates or ordered domains serve as domain-wall pinning sites.
Structural inhomogeneity associated with the secondary phase hinders domain-wall motion.
Hindering domain-wall motion through precipitate pinning increases the coercive field.
The aging treatment will increase coercivity relative to an untreated composition-matched control.
The coercive field may rise from no more than 100 Oe to several hundred Oe.
The precipitate-forming treatment can preserve high saturation magnetization without a significant reduction.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on precipitate volume fraction and spatial distribution.
Excessive phase transformation may reduce the overall saturation magnetization.
